passages.text: Insomnia, or sleeplessness, is a ____ complaint. When we are suffering from insomnia, we may have a wide range of ____ to deal with it. But what is ____ to many sufferers is their inability to relax fully and "switch the mind ____." Constant thoughts, ____ around and around in the mind, moving from one ____ to the next, prevent stillness and peace and intrude on our daily lives. The worried thoughts may ____ over trivial or serious matters, and they can be so overwhelming that the sufferer cannot fall asleep. As one famous writer, Charlotte Brontë, once wrote, "I ____ pity you for having had so many sleepless nights." Indeed, insomniacs are awake during the night and asleep during the ____. At night, they wake ____, worrying about what they should do, or what they should have done. In severe cases, a sufferer may sleep for only a few hours for ten nights ____, which amounts to only thirty hours ____ of sleep, without ____ at night. This will surely do great harm to one's health. Therefore, it is important for the sufferer to understand the causes of insomnia, which helps him or her know ____ why he or she is suffering from it. Meanwhile, the doctor and the patient should work together and communicate without missing a ____.

The modern world is very convenient, and many people may have already forgotten what life was like without it. In the U.S., the first European settlements were established along the eastern coast, starting in the early 1600s. The first Thanksgiving was celebrated by the Pilgrims in 1621 to give thanks for a successful harvest. Over the next century, thousands of settlers followed, and many colonies were established.

The first white settlers in the New World came from Spain. They settled in St. Augustine in 1565. Other settlements followed along the eastern coast. But the first permanent English settlement in America was founded at Jamestown, in Virginia, in 1607. In May 1607, three ships arrived at the coast of Virginia carrying 104 men. They were sent by the Virginia Company of London, which hoped to find gold and other valuable metals, as well as a route to the East Indies. The colonists chose a site on the James River, and built a fort there. During the first few years, the colonists suffered greatly from disease, famine, and conflicts with the local Indians. By the winter of 1609, known as the "starving time," only 60 of the original settlers were still alive. In 1619, the first Africans arrived in Virginia. Though they came as indentured servants at first, slavery soon became the legal system that would shape America's future. Meanwhile, the colonists learned to grow tobacco, which became the main cash crop of Virginia and saved the colony from economic failure.

I received a call from a college friend last week. We had not seen each other for six years since graduation. He was nervous when he made the phone call, because he had changed so much that he was afraid I would not recognize him. He remembered that he used to be a bookworm in college, having few friends except Jane, his best friend. Jane had changed his life by suggesting he join the student union and take part in social activities to develop his social skills. He followed her advice, and this marked the beginning of a new chapter in his life. He became popular and successful. He said that if it had not been for Jane's words that day, he would not be what he was today.

In the summer of 1859, a man watched his son practicing handwriting. The son was about to give up because he had made little progress, though he had been practicing for a long time. The father told his son a story about his own childhood: how he had been weak in studies and had been looked down upon, but how he had kept trying and finally succeeded. He encouraged his son to keep on practicing and never give up. Years later, the son became a famous writer. Actually, the father in the story was a poor farmer who could barely read or write himself. When asked why he had told his son that story, he said, "I did not know how to teach him, but I knew that if he kept on trying, he would succeed one day." The story tells us that success comes from perseverance.

questions.stem: For this part, you are supposed to write an essay in English in about 100~120 words based on the following news in Chinese. Write your essay on the Answer Sheet. 王明的妈妈由于工作忙，没有时间去商场购物，于是让王明帮她在网上买了一件衣服。货到后，妈妈发现衣服不但款式漂亮，而且价格便宜，非常高兴。请你根据以上内容，以"Online Shopping"为题，用英语写一篇短文。内容包括：1. 上述新闻内容；2. 网上购物的利与弊。
questions.answer:
范文：
Online Shopping

Online shopping is becoming more and more popular in our daily life. Last week, Wang Ming's mother asked him to buy a dress for her because she was too busy to go shopping in the mall. When the dress arrived, she was very happy to find that it was beautiful and cheap.

Online shopping has many advantages. First of all, it is very convenient. We can buy almost everything without going out. Besides, goods online are usually cheaper than those in stores. However, every coin has two sides. Online shopping also has disadvantages. We can't see the goods in person, so sometimes what we get is different from what we see online.

In a word, online shopping brings us both convenience and problems.
questions.explanation: 写作要点：1. 转述新闻内容（王明帮妈妈网购衣服，物美价廉，妈妈很高兴）；2. 分析网上购物的利（方便、便宜）与弊（看不到实物、可能与实物不符）。
